purpose: BROWNFIELD EXAMPLE. The spec extracted from code/legacy-cart/cart.js — code that already existed, with a threshold nobody documented, a rejection nobody tested, and one line that turned out to be dead. Shows the three things only brownfield can do: declare a substitution boundary, account for every decision site in the implementation, and measure fidelity against the original instead of asserting it.

excluded.reason: Totals here count quantities; money is the billing area's.
Nothing in this code reserves stock; adding an item does not hold it.

boundary.persistence_contract: The store's cart shape IS the contract — existing carts must remain readable. A replacement may change how it talks to the store, not what a stored cart looks like.
free: how items are looked up (find vs index)
error class names, as long as the call still throws

entities.name: Cart
entities.description: CLOSED, read off the code: `status` is only ever compared to "checked_out" and only ever assigned it. Anything else a regenerated implementation invents (Abandoned, Locked) would be new behavior nobody specified.

externals.name: PaymentGateway
externals.description: Charged at checkout. The code's try/catch says more about it than any document did.

outcomes.name: DECLINED
outcomes.description: Explicitly refused; the cart stays open.

outcomes.name: UNAVAILABLE
outcomes.description: Threw — timeout or transport. The charge may or may not have landed.

assumptions.statement: A charge that throws did not take the money, so retrying is safe.
assumptions.rationale: The code retries on UNAVAILABLE with no idempotency key, so a landed-but-unacknowledged charge would double-charge. Carried as risk because it is what the existing system already does — extracting the spec did not create this exposure, it revealed it. Tracked in Q-002.
assumptions.discharged_by: Nothing today. A gateway idempotency key would discharge it.

open_questions.question: What should adding an item to a full cart do — throw as today, or return a result the UI can render? The code throws, which no requirement describes.
Retry after a thrown charge assumes the money did not move (ASM-001). Should checkout send an idempotency key before we rely on that?
Checkout of an empty cart THROWS while declined and unavailable RETURN ok:false. Is the inconsistency intentional?
clear() is implemented and unspecified. Is it product behavior, or a leftover from an admin tool?

states.name: CheckedOut
states.description: Frozen; INV-001 keeps its items fixed.
